title: Job seeker calls for ban on 'ghost' interviews that harvest data for AI
key_facts: New Zealand job seeker Charlie Maclean was interviewed by an AI interview agent for a remote role advertised on LinkedIn, with timed answers, and was then ghosted by the company.
She suspects the listing was a 'ghost' job used to harvest personal data to train AI, and has launched a petition to Parliament to ban such advertisements.
Victoria University organisational psychology lecturer Ben Walker says there is no 'case-closed' evidence but enough online commentary to suspect some listings are spurious.
Recruiters RNZ spoke to had not seen ghost jobs in New Zealand but had heard of the practice overseas; Tribe Group chief executive Bruce Pilbrow called the scenario plausible.
AI lecturer Andrew Lensen says CVs hold valuable personal data and concern is growing over where it ends up.
LinkedIn told RNZ it is investing in free verifications and that every job must be authentic; SEEK and Trade Me said ghost jobs are not a material issue on their sites.
Companies accused in online threads did not respond to RNZ.
quote_evidence: After some digging online, she fears the company that sent an AI agent to interview her was simply after her personal data to train artificial intelligence - a potential scam or so-called "ghost" job, a scenario where a company advertises for a role it has no intention of filling.
"There's a lot happening in the AI space and the online space in the sense of harvesting information," he said. "Data is king."
why_it_matters_hint: A petition and expert comment on suspected fake AI-run job interviews used to gather candidates' data, with no proven case yet.
notes: Suspicion, not a proven scam; experts say evidence is anecdotal.
